I just need to know what changes should be made there to adjust for the montgomery form. https://github.com/NethermindEth/bandersnatch-sharp/tree/main/src/Bandersnatch/Nethermind.Verkle.Polynomial Hey Tanish, you should be able to test the Montgomery implementation separately from the rest of the code (it’s a way to internally represent a field element, such that modular arithmetic is faster) I’d probably just skip that for now and implement the higher level parts for now Since it’s not a blocker I implemented everything and everything is working fine - its just part required for proofs that started failing after I switched to the montgomery implementation. there might be some changes that are needed when we use the montgomery form with polynomials. like with the scalar multiplication in ExtendedPoint - after switching I need to covert the scalar back to normal representation before the multiplication. Oh I see, you only ever need to come out of Montgomery form when you need to operate on the actual value of the field element, so this is the case for scalar multiplication and any toBytes methods where you want to convert the field element to a byte array Looking at the code; could you show me where the file is for Montgomery tests? Im on mobile, so I may have missed them i dont have any tests for that, all the modules are using the montogery implementation now. so the test for polynomials are here: https://github.com/NethermindEth/bandersnatch-sharp/blob/main/src/Bandersnatch/Nethermind.Verkle.Polynomial.Test/MonomialBasisTests.cs https://github.com/NethermindEth/bandersnatch-sharp/blob/main/src/Bandersnatch/Nethermind.Verkle.Polynomial.Test/LagrangeBasisTests.cs the test that are commented out are failing - interpolation and vanishing polynomial. ahh okay, so technically when we use the double and add in scalar multiplication and we check for bits, we are checking on the byte array, so there also we should use the normal form. i changed it in the toBytes func but didnt do it there, that might be the issue, will have a look. thanks!
